slides.label: The Takeover
slides.text: If you've been to a party, a barbershop or a car on *Dyckman*, you've heard "Dame Hombro," now *No. 10* on Billboard's Hot Latin Songs.

slides.label: Who He Is
slides.text: Bulin 47, real name *Hancel Teodoro Vargas Reynoso*, started with comedy videos before dembow took over his life.

slides.label: Hometown & Age
slides.text: He's from *Santo Domingo*. His age? Spotify says he's *31*, born 1995, but one database lists 1989 instead.

slides.label: The Rise
slides.text: He blew up with comedy clips in 2016, dropped *El Rey de las Dagor* in 2017, then turned headliner in 2021 with "Bajo Mundo."

slides.label: Biggest Hits
slides.text: From *"Bajo Mundo"* to *"Calorazo"* (66M+ YouTube views) to "CELOS" with Tokischa, the hits kept stacking.

slides.label: Who He Runs With
slides.text: His day one is *Ceky Viciny*. He's also linked up with *Tokischa, Arcángel, El Alfa* and even 6ix9ine.

slides.label: Next Up
slides.text: December 26, 2026: Bulin 47 brings the *Dame Hombro World Tour* to the *United Palace* in Washington Heights.

slides.label: The Moment
slides.text: It's the only date on his Spotify page right now, so if you want "Dame Hombro" live in NYC, this is the night.

Bulin 47's "Dame Hombro" just hit No. 10 on Billboard's Hot Latin Songs, and if you've been anywhere near Dyckman, you already knew.

Real name Hancel Teodoro Vargas Reynoso, he started out making comedy videos before dembow took over his life. Now he's got 26 million Spotify plays on this one track alone, a video closing in on 100 million YouTube views, and collabs with Tokischa, Arcángel, El Alfa and even 6ix9ine.

His age is still up for debate (Spotify says 1995, one database says 1989), but one thing isn't: on December 26, he brings "Dame Hombro" home to the United Palace in Washington Heights, and as of now, it's the only date on his calendar.

caption_linkedin:
Bulin 47 didn't start as a music star, he started as a comedian making videos for laughs. Now his song "Dame Hombro" with Kevin Wai sits at No. 10 on Billboard's Hot Latin Songs, with 26 million Spotify plays and a video nearing 100 million YouTube views.

The throughline is consistency. Comedic clips in 2016, an album a year later, a turn to headliner status in 2021 with "Bajo Mundo" and a collab with El Alfa, then years of steady singles, several a year, keeping him in rotation until the breakout hit landed.

That's the quiet lesson in his rise: staying visible, staying releasing, long before the charts caught up.

On December 26 he plays the United Palace in Washington Heights, his only scheduled date right now.
